lines.text: Ticketing is 12% of Live Nation's sales. Nearly half its profit.
lines.say: Ticketing is twelve percent of Live Nation's sales. Nearly half its profit.

lines.text: In 2025, ticketing earned $1.1 billion in adjusted operating income on $3.1 billion of revenue.
lines.say: In twenty twenty-five, ticketing earned one point one billion dollars in adjusted operating income on three point one billion of revenue.

lines.text: That's about a 37% margin. Concerts kept 3.3%.
lines.say: That's about a thirty-seven percent margin. Concerts kept three point three percent.

lines.text: The trick is volume: 346 million fee-bearing tickets in 2025, roughly $3.28 of profit each.

post.title: Ticketing: 12% of Live Nation's sales, ~half its profit
post.ig:
Ticketing is 12% of Live Nation's sales. Nearly half its profit.

In 2025, the Ticketing segment made $1.1B in adjusted operating income on $3.1B of revenue, a margin near 37% (concerts: 3.3%).
Ticketmaster says it typically keeps about $5 of a $100 all-in ticket; it sold 346M fee-bearing tickets in 2025.
An FTC rule requiring all-in ticket prices took effect May 12, 2025. In April 2026 a jury in the states' antitrust case found Live Nation liable; the companies are challenging the verdict (status as of Sept 2026).

Sources: Live Nation FY2025 10-K and results, FTC (16 CFR 464), court reporting (CNN, Music Business Worldwide).
News and education, not financial advice.

post.yt_desc:
In 2025, Live Nation's Ticketing segment (Ticketmaster) made $1.1 billion in adjusted operating income on $3.1 billion of revenue, about 12% of company sales but nearly half its adjusted operating income, across 346 million fee-bearing tickets. The FTC's all-in pricing rule for live-event tickets took effect May 12, 2025, and as of September 2026 the companies were challenging an April 2026 jury verdict in the states' antitrust case. Sources: Live Nation FY2025 10-K, FTC 16 CFR 464, CNN.

News and education, not financial advice.
